subject: How long do interaction artifacts live? (requests vs generated content)
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@brightbank.com>

Subject: Quick question on how long you keep interaction artifacts

Hi Neha,

We're evaluating Redwood for BrightBank's chat assistant pilot and the security/privacy team has a quick question: for the hosted API, what are the default storage windows for (1) request payloads/user inputs, (2) model-generated outputs, and (3) any intermediate/streamed fragments or KV-cache artifacts?

They want a short, clear mapping for our procurement packet — ideally a single-paragraph answer and any references to a follow-up runbook if we need proof of deletion. Also, do EU-region customers get a different default?

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Security Architect, BrightBank

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the question. Short answer for your packet: by default we retain request payloads (user inputs) for 30 days, model-generated outputs for 30 days, and streaming fragments/KV cache are not persisted beyond the live inference session unless the customer explicitly enables session archival; EU-region hosted customers get the same default retention but records are stored in EU data centers when requested.

I'll loop in Karthik for a one-paragraph approved blurb and attach the runbook with proof-of-deletion steps. If you need a signed statement for procurement we can generate that after you confirm the account/region.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is an approved, concise mapping you can include in BrightBank's procurement packet. I've kept it non-legal/plain-English; if you need a signed addendum we can produce one after you confirm the BrightBank account/region.

Approved blurb (one paragraph):
By default Redwood retains request payloads (the raw user inputs submitted to our hosted API) for 30 days and model-generated outputs (final responses) for 30 days to support debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring. Streaming fragments (intermediate tokens/buffers) and inference-level KV cache are treated as ephemeral — they are kept in-memory for the duration of the live session and are not written to persistent logs unless the customer explicitly enables session archival or exports. For customers who require EU residency, records can be pinned to EU data centers; the same default retention windows apply but data residency and storage location will be confined to the EU region when configured.

Additional notes and controls:
- Customers can request earlier deletion or an account-wide retention shorter than default via their org settings; we provide a documented erasure runbook and proof-of-deletion artifacts on request.
- Attachments or uploaded files included in requests are retained according to the same schedule unless marked for separate storage (e.g., object storage with longer retention).
- For audit/incident needs we support export of deletion evidence (log hashes, job ids, and storage purge timestamps) — see the attached runbook for the standard procedure.

Attachments: default_retention_matrix.xlsx (summary table), customer_erasure_runbook.pdf (deletion evidence workflow).

If you want this shortened further into a single-sentence legal line or need a formal letterhead statement, reply and we will generate it.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
